newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity to hold meetings to reassure clients.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity to hold meetings to reassure clients.

text.p: Fidelity Investments, hit with declining market share, defections from its ranks of fund managers and poor returns over the last year, will hold meetings this month in six cities with its top clients.

"They want to reassure people that they are going to slow down the turnover of portfolio managers," said Donald Dion, publisher of Fidelity Independent Advisor. "They're trying to convince everyone that they have a very deep bench ... and they can handle the turnover they have experienced."
Fidelity executives also will tell their clients that the mutual funds are now sticking closer to their stated investment goals and styles, Dion said.

A Fidelity spokeswoman said the meetings will provide "our customers with an opportunity to participate in the personal exchange of information and insight with the individuals who are responsible for the investment management and business strategy at Fidelity."

Presentations will be given by Gary Burkhead, president of Fidelity Management & Research Co.; Paul Hondros, president of Fidelity's retail group; and Bob Reynolds, head of Fidelity's institutional retirement group.
Analysts said Magellan Fund manager Bob Stansky may also be at the meetings.
Since the beginning of December, four fund managers, including veterans Brian Posner, Larry Greenberg and Michael Gray, announced they would leave the company.
Greenberg's exit prompted Fidelity to switch managers at about 19 stock funds last week, the most sweeping change at Fidelity since last year.
Analysts said the managerial changes and poor performance last year at most of its diversified U.S. equity funds has spurred investors to cash out and caused Fidelity to lose market share.

The mutual fund industry enjoyed a cash inflow of around $13.5 billion into U.S. stock mutual funds in December, according to the Investment Company Institute, an industry group. But Fidelity lost cash during the month, analysts said.
David O'Leary, president of Alpha Equity Research, estimated that investors pulled out about $275 million from Fidelity's equity funds during the month.
Separately, Fidelity's massive Magellan Fund cut its exposure to stocks in November and raised cash in anticipation of investors pulling their money from the struggling mutual fund, analysts said.
"I think it may be an indication that they see a lot more withdrawals," O'Leary said. "They expect to continue to lose assets."

Magellan, the largest mutual fund in the country, cut its equity holdings to 88.5 percent of total assets at the end of November, the most recent month figures were available, from 89.8 percent at the end of October, according the the monthly Fidelity fund guide.
Magellan manager Stansky raised the fund's holdings in cash to 3.6 percent of assets from 1.5 percent and trimmmed bonds to 7.9 percent from 8.7 percent.
O'Leary estimated that investors pulled out more than $760 million from Magellan during December and around $5 billion from the $54 billion fund last year.
Eric Kobren, publisher of Fidelity Insight, estimated that another $500 million had been pulled out of Magellan so far in January.
Fidelity declined to discuss cash flows.

Investors also pulled more than $200 million from the $15.2 billion Fidelity Equity-Income II Fund during December after fund manager Brian Posner announced his resignation to join E.M. Warburg Pincus & Co., O'Leary said.
"It's possible that the money switched from Fidelity to Warburg Pincus following Posner," O'Leary said. "That's the worst of situations if the money starts following the managers."
